the majority of students in the UK do not have the necessary knowledge, values, and behaviors for successful global citizenship.
the internationalisation of the curriculum is a process that involves all stakeholders in the university and that the process of change is not easy and takes a long time to implement.

the ways in which internationalising the curriculum can be understood as an ethical project.
how the curriculum can help students develop the knowledge, values and behaviours that will enable them to negotiate the challenges of a complex, interdependent, globalised world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the curriculum is a key component of the internationalisation agenda, and that internationalisation is not only about international students, but also about the majority of students in higher education, and the curriculum should be designed with this in mind.

the globalisation of the economy, the increasing mobility of people and the development of new information and communication technologies have created a world in which the concept of the nation-state is increasingly challenged and where the concept of a national culture is becoming less relevant.
the internationalization process is a complex and challenging task that requires the participation and support of all stakeholders.

we are working to develop a curriculum that will help our students become more aware of themselves as global citizens.

internationalisation at home requires a commitment to a new set of values, new knowledge and new behaviours.
internationalising the curriculum means more than just teaching about international issues, and more than just teaching in an international context.
